title: 11th Word: Construction of the Palace and Appointment of the Explaining Master

questions.question: What major project did the king begin after deciding to show his greatness and treasures?
questions.answer: He began building a huge, impressive palace.

questions.question: How did the king make the palace beautiful and valuable?
questions.answer: He filled it with precious decorations, fine artwork, and skillful design.

questions.question: What did the king prepare for the people after finishing the palace?
questions.answer: He prepared wide dining tables with many kinds of delicious food and blessings.

questions.question: How were the tables arranged for the guests?
questions.answer: Each group was given a suitable table.

questions.question: Why did the king invite people from all parts of his land?
questions.answer: He wanted them to eat and also to look at the palace and its display.

questions.question: Who did the king appoint after inviting the people?
questions.answer: He appointed a highest-ranking commander to teach the people.

questions.question: What was one main duty of that teacher?
questions.answer: He was to explain the purpose of the palace and the meaning of what was inside it.

questions.question: Besides explaining the palace, what else was the teacher supposed to make known?
questions.answer: He was to describe the maker, explain the secrets of the decorations, and show what the artworks pointed to.

questions.question: What did the teacher help visitors understand about the jewels and designs?
questions.answer: He helped them see that these showed the owner’s perfection and artistic skill.

questions.question: What practical guidance did the teacher give the people about visiting the palace?
questions.answer: He taught them the proper way to behave and the ceremonies the king wanted.

questions.question: Did the teacher work completely alone in every part of the palace, or was help given to him?
questions.answer: He had helpers in each section of the palace.

questions.question: Where was the teacher himself when he addressed the people?
questions.answer: He was in the largest room among his students, making an announcement to everyone there.

questions.question: What does the palace itself show about the king’s intentions?
questions.answer: It shows that he wanted to display his riches, skill, wisdom, and knowledge in a grand way.

questions.question: What can we infer from the king decorating the palace with treasures from his own stores?
questions.answer: It suggests that the palace was meant to reveal what belonged to him and to show his excellence.

questions.question: Why is it important that the king set out food as well as decorations?
questions.answer: It shows that the guests were not only meant to look, but also to receive generosity and care.

questions.question: What does giving each group its own fitting table suggest about the king?
questions.answer: It suggests that he was organized, thoughtful, and generous to different people.

questions.question: Why would the people need a teacher in such a palace?
questions.answer: They needed someone to explain what they were seeing so they would not miss the real meaning.

questions.question: What does the appointment of a supreme commander as teacher show about the importance of the message?
questions.answer: It shows that the message was serious, official, and central to the whole palace.

questions.question: According to the passage, was the teacher’s job only to describe objects, or also to teach their deeper meaning?
questions.answer: He was to do both, especially to teach their deeper meaning.

questions.question: What connection did the teacher make between the beauty of the palace and the owner?
questions.answer: He showed that the beauty and artistry of the palace pointed to the owner’s perfections and skills.

questions.question: Why did the people need to be taught the correct manners for viewing the palace?
questions.answer: Because the king had a desired way for his guests to respond to what they saw.

questions.question: What does the presence of assistants in every area tell us about the palace?
questions.answer: It tells us that the palace was very large and needed guidance throughout.

questions.question: Why did the teacher stay in the largest apartment while his assistants were in other areas?
questions.answer: It suggests that he was the main instructor and the center of the teaching.

questions.question: In your own words, describe the palace the king built.
questions.answer: It was a large, splendid place with many rooms, rich decorations, and carefully arranged beauty.

questions.question: What two things were especially spread through the palace to impress the guests?
questions.answer: Valuable ornaments and beautifully prepared food.

questions.question: How does the passage show that the banquet was extremely generous?
questions.answer: It says the meal included many kinds of delicious things and was arranged with great care and richness.

questions.question: Why were people called from all over the kingdom instead of only from one place?
questions.answer: The invitation was wide because the king wanted all his subjects to witness the display and enjoy the feast.

questions.question: What was the teacher expected to explain about the decorations?
questions.answer: He was expected to explain their hidden meanings and the secrets behind them.

questions.question: What did the teacher teach about the arts found in the palace?
questions.answer: He taught what those arts were indicating about the owner.

questions.question: Why did visitors need instruction about official ceremonies?
questions.answer: They needed to know how the unseen king wanted things to be done.

questions.question: What do the words about the king not appearing directly suggest about the teacher’s role?
questions.answer: They suggest that the teacher was necessary as the one who conveyed the king’s will to the people.

questions.question: How was the teaching organized across the palace?
questions.answer: The main teacher stayed in the central large room, and helpers served in the other sections.

questions.question: What happened first in the passage: the appointment of the teacher or the preparation of the banquet?
questions.answer: The banquet and palace arrangements came first, and the teacher was appointed later.

questions.question: What kinds of things did the king use to decorate the palace?
questions.answer: He used jewels, beautiful crafted works, and carefully arranged decorations.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the king’s own involvement in the palace’s beauty?
questions.answer: It shows that he personally adorned it with skillful works.

questions.question: How did wisdom and knowledge appear in the palace?
questions.answer: They appeared in the careful order, subtle design, and remarkable crafted details.

questions.question: What was the purpose of inviting the people to the palace?
questions.answer: It was for them to enjoy the feast and see the great display.

questions.question: What title or position was given to the one who would teach the people?
questions.answer: He was made the chief commander and instructor.

questions.question: Name two responsibilities of the teacher.
questions.answer: He had to explain the palace’s purpose and teach what the decorations and arts were showing.

questions.question: What did the teacher explain about the relationship between the palace and its owner?
questions.answer: He explained that what was in the palace pointed to the owner’s qualities and excellence.

questions.question: Why did the teacher explain proper behavior, not just information?
questions.answer: Because understanding alone was not enough; the guests also needed to act in the right way.

questions.question: What can we understand from the teacher’s assistants being placed in each part of the palace?
questions.answer: Guidance was meant to reach visitors everywhere in the palace.

questions.question: What did the teacher do while staying in the largest room?
questions.answer: He addressed all the spectators with an announcement.

questions.question: What big idea connects the building, decorating, feeding, and teaching in this passage?
questions.answer: All of them serve the purpose of showing the king’s greatness and helping people understand it.

questions.question: Why is the palace described as both vast and majestic?
questions.answer: To show that it was not ordinary, but built to display greatness and inspire wonder.

questions.question: How does the passage show both beauty and planning in the palace?
questions.answer: It describes fine ornaments and also careful arrangement, wise order, and suitable placement.

questions.question: What does the rich banquet add to the meaning of the palace?
questions.answer: It shows the king’s generosity along with his power and artistry.

questions.question: Why would each group have its own fitting table instead of everyone being treated exactly the same way?
questions.answer: It suggests that the king provided in a way suited to different groups and situations.

questions.question: What was the teacher supposed to help people understand about the maker of the palace?
questions.answer: He was to help them know who the maker was and recognize the qualities shown in the palace.

questions.question: What is the difference between simply seeing the jewels and understanding them rightly?
questions.answer: Seeing notices their appearance, but understanding sees what they reveal about the owner.

questions.question: Why did the king need an instructor if the palace was already full of signs of greatness?
questions.answer: Because people might look without understanding unless someone explained the meanings.

questions.question: What does the teacher’s role tell us about the guests?
questions.answer: It tells us the guests needed guidance in both understanding and behavior.

questions.question: How do the assistants support the teacher’s mission?
questions.answer: They carry the teaching throughout the palace so people in every area can be guided.

questions.question: What is the importance of the final announcement mentioned at the end of the passage?
questions.answer: It prepares for the main message that the spectators are supposed to hear and follow.

questions.question: Summarize the passage in one or two sentences.
questions.answer: A king built and richly decorated a great palace, prepared a generous feast, and invited his people. Then he appointed a chief teacher, with helpers, to explain the palace, its meanings, and the proper way to respond.

questions.question: What details in the passage show the king’s generosity?
questions.answer: He spread many kinds of excellent food, invited people from all over, and arranged fitting tables for different groups.

questions.question: What details show the king’s skill and wisdom?
questions.answer: The palace was beautifully adorned, carefully ordered, and filled with meaningful artistic works.

questions.question: Why is the teacher called both a teacher and an instructor in meaning?
questions.answer: Because he was not only giving facts but also training the people how to understand and behave.

questions.question: What hidden aspect of the palace was the teacher supposed to uncover?
questions.answer: He was supposed to uncover the purposes, secrets, and meanings behind what the people saw.

questions.question: What did the teacher explain about the artistic works inside the palace?
questions.answer: He explained what they pointed to and how they reflected the owner’s qualities.

questions.question: What did the teacher explain about proper conduct?
questions.answer: He taught the manners and ceremonial behavior the king wanted from visitors.

questions.question: Why is it important that the king did not appear directly in this part of the story?
questions.answer: It makes the teacher’s explanation necessary for the people to know the king’s wishes.

questions.question: What can we infer from the teacher remaining in the largest apartment among his students?
questions.answer: He held the central place of leadership in teaching and gave the main message from there.

questions.question: What overall lesson about understanding appearances can be taken from this passage?
questions.answer: Beautiful things should not be looked at only on the surface; they should be understood for the deeper meanings they carry.

questions.question: How does this passage prepare the reader for what comes next?
questions.answer: It sets up the speaker’s announcement by showing why the people need guidance to understand the palace correctly.
